LESSON: INTRODUCTION TO SOCIAL ENTREPRENEURSHIP

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: COMMUNITY SERVICE LEARNING FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE
Strand: Social Entrepreneurship
Topic 4.1: Introduction to Social Entrepreneurship
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 6

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Introduction to Social Entrepreneurship, part of Social Entrepreneurship in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 COMMUNITY SERVICE LEARNING FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE.

Key inquiry question: How can social entrepreneurship promote the welfare of a community?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Introduction to Social Entrepreneurship together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and collaboration: Learners speak clearly and engagingly while reflecting on benefits of social

entrepreneurship in the community

● Digital literacy: Learners use digital devices with assistive technology to search differences between social

enterprise and other enterprises.

Values:
Respect: Learner respect divergent opinions while discussing the concept of social entrepreneurship.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Online safety: Learners observe online safety while searching using digital devices with assistive technology on the

differences between social enterprise and other enterprises.

Suggested learning resources:

Digital devices with assistive technology, appropriate audio-visual clips on entrepreneurship, Braille course books,

Print course books, braille and print writing materials, manila paper, and mark pens of contrasting colours.
